A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same lower-bound research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. V1 Appendices A–D correspond largely to v2 Appendices C–F; the proof sketch moves to Appendix A, and Appendix B adds related work.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical constructions, bounds, and proofs, including its appendices. Figure 1 illustrates analytically defined functions; no original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its additions concern proofs, formal protocols, and discussion, without original empirical results.

M1.justification: The stochastic oracle used in the lower-bound construction changes: Equation (26) replaces the Bernoulli-mask condition j > prog1(x) with j = progK(x) + 1, altering responses for inputs with gaps in their support. The hard function and optimization updates remain unchanged. Bidirectional communication already appeared in v1 Protocol 2.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical benchmarks. The added discussion of convex, finite-sum, and other optimization settings concerns related work, not newly evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: SGD, Batch Synchronized SGD, and Batch QSGD retain their roles as theoretical complexity comparisons. Appendix B's additional cited methods are not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies empirical evaluation protocols. Changes to the communication protocol and stochastic oracle concern the formal lower-bound construction, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies. The new oracle and communication remarks are theoretical arguments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The analytical concentration bounds are retained; the explicit i.i.d. oracle notation is not repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. The principal time-complexity bounds in Equations (5), (11), and (12), their scaling conclusions, and Figure 1's function curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 and v1 Lemma B.4, now D.4, replace a maximum-coordinate bound with a stronger support-inclusion statement and revise its proof. Equation (26) changes the oracle construction. Remarks E.1, E.2, and F.2 address shared-randomness queries and positive communication costs in the previously ignored direction. These are targeted mathematical revisions supporting the retained lower-bound rates.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same limited-scalability claim. Section 6 newly claims that the worst-case bounds also apply to methods using biased compressors, extending the stated applicability beyond v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 adds an explicit regime where worker-side compression can still help when server-to-worker communication is cheaper. Section 6 newly identifies convexity and second-order smoothness as assumptions that might permit escaping the bound. Existing limitations concerning logarithmic factors and random sparsifiers remain.

D1.justification: The unified Protocol 1 explicitly specifies i.i.d. gradient draws, admissible query and message supports, and processing arriving vectors before simultaneous queries. These add operational precision to v1's protocols. No implementation, hardware, or code/data-access information is introduced.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially broadens the literature positioning to convex lower bounds, graph oracles, delayed optimization, variance reduction, finite-sum problems, and local/intermittent communication methods. It adds ten cited works and explicitly distinguishes the related convex minimax results of Woodworth et al. from this paper's compression-and-scalability question.

P1.justification: The proof sketch moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix A, supporting appendices are renumbered, and the notation glossary is expanded. V2 also adds related-work and acknowledgement sections and updates affiliations and conference headers. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V1's two protocol displays are consolidated into an expanded Protocol 1. Figure 1 retains its plots but corrects the derivative named in its caption from Phi-prime to Psi-prime. Conference headers and text reflow alter the layout without adding result figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The revised oracle and stronger support lemma improve the precision of the central coordinate-discovery argument. Explicit communication-cost arguments, clearer protocol details, and broader related-work discussion also help readers assess the retained bounds. Section 6's new assertion that unbiased compressors contain biased compressors is poorly justified against Definition 1.5, tempering these gains. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement rather than a new scientific result.
